description: Works out the dates Awaab’s Law gives a council or housing association in England (the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025, SI 2025/1042) to deal with damp or mould: investigate it, give the tenant a written summary, finish any safety work and start any further work. It counts working days from the day after the landlord found out, leaving out weekends and bank holidays in England and Wales, and says whether each date has passed. For an emergency hazard it gives the 24-hour rule; for other hazards it gives the position on Awaab’s Law Phase 2 from the site’s legal register. It says when Awaab’s Law does not apply (private landlords, Wales, shared ownership and long leases). It does not decide whether a hazard is significant, and a missed date is a dated failure, not an entitlement to anything.

asAt.description: Work it out as at this date instead of today in England (YYYY-MM-DD).

awareOn.description: Damp or mould: the day the landlord found out, usually the day it was first reported (in writing, if it was) (YYYY-MM-DD).

hazard.description: For a council or housing association: "damp_mould", "emergency" (something putting someone in immediate danger, such as a gas leak or exposed live wiring) or "other" (another problem, such as a broken boiler, a broken window or unsafe stairs).

investigatedOn.description: Damp or mould: the day the landlord’s investigation finished, if it has. Leave out if it has not investigated, or if not known (YYYY-MM-DD).

landlord.description: Who the landlord is: "council" or "housing_association" (in England), "private" (a private landlord or letting agent), "wales" (any landlord in Wales) or "ownership" (the tenant owns a share, or has a long lease).

title: Awaab’s Law deadline checker
